messages:
incident-bot: PAGING: sustained p99 latency spike on /v1/embeddings (eu-west-2). p95=1.9s (SLO=0.8s), p99=7.6s. streaming/async sessions experiencing stalls and reconnects. customer-impact=medium-high. triggered at 21:06 UTC. oncall paged.
frank: oncall here, pulling up traces and ASG health. any deploys? not seeing app deploys.
grace: No deployments. Observability: DNS lookup times for egress resolvers rose from 12ms -> 68ms around 21:04. Also seeing a jump in retransmits and out-of-order packets across eu-west-2b -> eu-west-2c paths.
hannah: Proxy metrics: accept queue latency climbing, backend->egress connections in TIME_WAIT increased dramatically. Could be connection churn at NAT or a routing asymmetry.
ian: I will take network. quick netstat and conntrack snapshots incoming.
netops-bot: Auto-checks: nat-a (eu-west-2a) conntrack=320k (limit 500k), nat-b conntrack=980k (limit 1.0M), nat-c conntrack=1.05M (limit 1.05M). nat-c reports 98% conntrack usage. BGP peer health nominal. inter-AZ RTT 8ms -> 120ms for some flows.
frank: nat-c at conntrack limit — that explains handshake failures. are sessions being re-routed to nat-c due to transient failure on nat-b? need exact egress mapping.
grace: Querying request routing: many streaming sessions from GPU-pool-eu-w2b are offloading to nat-c after a health probe flakiness on nat-b. healthcheck flaps recorded at 21:03:58 for nat-b (probe timeouts).
hannah: Logs show repeated TLS timeouts: "tls: handshake timeout" and many SYN retransmits. clients retry which increases short-lived connections and fills conntrack.
ian: Hypothesis: probe-induced failover moved heavy streaming egress to nat-c, which hit conntrack ceiling -> SYN/handshake losses -> clients retry -> cascading stalls and p99 tail.
frank: Mitigations: (A) rebalance egress by flipping route table association for affected subnets off nat-c back to nat-b (fast), (B) temporarily increase conntrack limit on nat-c if possible, (C) divert streaming control plane to a fallback regional path (config). I propose A + B.
grace: Agree. We'll perform a subset route-table reassociation as canary and also bump conntrack sysctl on nat-c nodes.
ian: Playing commands now. Step 1: increase conntrack max on nat-c nodes (sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=1500000) — applying via ssh-run across nat-c fleet.
netops-bot: conntrack increase applied to nat-c-1, nat-c-2. new conntrack counts: nat-c=1.15M, limit=1.5M.
hannah: Now doing route-table reassociation for two subnets to prefer nat-b. Using infra orchestration to flip associations for rtb-0bcde111 and rtb-0bcde112 as canary.
frank: Canary live. monitoring handshakes and p99 on canary-subset.
grace: Canary metrics (90s): canary p99 down from 7.6s -> 1.3s; global cluster p99 down to 2.8s. streaming stalls metric reduced on canary. non-canary still elevated.
ian: Noticed an unrelated DNS resolver pool node (res-02) had high mutex contention due to flood of client retries. Restarting res-02 now to clear resolver queue.
frank: After restart of res-02, DNS medians normalized. overall p95 now 0.92s, p99 1.8s. tail stalls dropping to ~1.5%.
grace: Customers impacted: ticketing shows two mid-market customers with streaming interruptions and one enterprise with retries on embedding calls. CS notified; advising status update.
hannah: Additional mitigations to avoid recurrence: make healthcheck sensitivity less aggressive to avoid failover on transient probe noise; autoscale NAT pool capacity when conntrack > 70%; add egress-balancer to distribute new connections more evenly.
ian: Recording commands used for rollback/mitigation:
```
# increase conntrack
sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=1500000
# re-associate route table
aws ec2 replace-route-table-association --association-id rtbassoc-0zzzz --route-table-id rtb-0bcde112
# restart dns resolver
systemctl restart resolver-service@res-02
```
frank: I'll keep the incident channel open until we're stable for 1h. if p99 > 3s or streaming_stall_rate > 5% re-pager to netops.
netops-bot: Post-mitigation checks: handshake success rate restored to 99.7%; packet retransmit rate reduced to baseline; conntrack headroom restored across nat fleet.
grace: Opening incident ticket IMP-2026-43712 for RCA: topics - probe flapping caused egress consolidation, conntrack exhaustion, DNS resolver contention, runbook gaps. Proposed follow-ups: adjust probe thresholds, add conntrack autoscale, add egress-balancer, improve DNS resolver redundancy, update paging thresholds for conntrack saturation.
julie: I'll own the postmortem and follow-ups. assigning tasks: netops to implement autoscale; infra to template conntrack bump; devex to update runbook and run drills.
frank: oncall handoff: my shift ends in 20m. julie, if stable can you take over? otherwise i'll stay on.
julie: taking over if stable; will monitor dashboards and confirm RCA timeline in morning. thanks team. :white_check_mark:
